Worked Example: A Puddle on a Sunny Day

components.label: WORKED EXAMPLE
components.title: What happens to a roadside puddle after the rain stops?
components.Body: 1. The rain stops and leaves a puddle of liquid water on the pavement.`n2. Throughout the afternoon, the sun provides thermal energy.`n3. Water molecules at the surface absorb enough energy to break free into the air as invisible water vapor.`n4. Over time, the puddle disappears entirely because all its water has evaporated into the atmosphere.
components.takeaway: Energy from the sun is the primary engine driving every phase change in the global water cycle.

components.title: Did you know?
components.text: The total amount of water on Earth is fixed and constantly recycled. The water from your tap today might have been swallowed by a dinosaur millions of years ago!

questions.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapor?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the process where liquid water absorbs heat from the sun and changes into water vapor.

questions.question: When water vapor cools down high in the atmosphere, what does it form?
questions.explanation: Cooling water vapor condenses around tiny particles in the air to form clouds.

questions.question: Which of the following is a form of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Rain, snow, sleet, and hail are all forms of precipitation that fall back to Earth.
